2608.03154.title: ANCHOR-RE: An Agentic Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Grounded Biomedical Relation Extraction
2608.03154.paper_summary: Biomedical relation extraction (BioRE) extracts structured knowledge from biomedical literature for applications such as knowledge base construction and hypothesis generation. Traditional symbolic systems such as SemRep provide high precision but limited recall, while large language models (LLMs) offer stronger contextual reasoning but remain prone to false-positive predictions. We developed ANCHOR-RE, a framework that integrates ontology-guided reasoning, external knowledge grounding, and data-driven verification rules into LLM inference. We evaluated it on three BioRE benchmarks (SemRepGS, DDI, and ChemProt) using both proprietary and open-weight LLMs. To assess generalizability beyond benchmark datasets while reducing potential evaluation bias from LLM pretraining contamination, we conducted a temporal evaluation using 100 biomedical articles published in 2026. With the proprietary backbone, ANCHOR-RE outperformed direct LLM prompting, improving micro-F1 from 0.654 to 0.676 on SemRepGS, from 0.769 to 0.872 on DDI, and from 0.939 to 0.941 on ChemProt. On DDI and ChemProt, it also outperformed previously reported inference-only methods and approached fine-tuned or instruction-tuned systems without parameter updates. Similar performance gains observed with open-weight LLMs indicate that the benefits were not limited to the proprietary backbone. On the post-cutoff set, manual assessment of 500 randomly sampled predictions yielded a precision of 69%, maintaining consistent precision on previously unseen biomedical literature. Neuro-symbolic reasoning can improve the reliability of LLM-based BioRE without fine-tuning. Results across multiple benchmarks, model families, and post-cutoff literature support ANCHOR-RE as a practical training-free approach to biomedical literature mining.
2608.03154.paper_summary_zh: 生物醫學關係提取（BioRE）從生物醫學文獻中提取結構化知識，用於知識庫建設和假設生成等應用。傳統的符號系統如SemRep提供高精度但回憶有限，而大型語言模型（LLMs）則提供更強的上下文推理能力，但仍然容易出現假陽性預測。我們開發了ANCHOR-RE，一個將本體導向推理、外部知識基礎和數據驅動驗證規則整合到LLM推理中的框架。我們在三個BioRE基準（SemRepGS、DDI和ChemProt）上評估了它，使用了專有和開放權重的LLM。為了評估其在基準數據集之外的可泛化性，同時減少來自LLM預訓練污染的潛在評估偏見，我們使用2026年發表的100篇生物醫學文章進行了時間評估。在專有骨幹上，ANCHOR-RE的表現超過了直接的LLM提示，將SemRepGS的微F1從0.654提高到0.676，將DDI從0.769提高到0.872，將ChemProt從0.939提高到0.941。在DDI和ChemProt上，它的表現也超過了之前報告的僅推理方法，並接近於無需參數更新的微調或指令微調系統。開放權重的LLM觀察到的類似性能增益表明，這些好處並不僅限於專有骨幹。在截止後數據集上，對500個隨機抽樣預測的手動評估產生了69%的精度，並在之前未見過的生物醫學文獻中保持了一致的精度。神經符號推理可以在不進行微調的情況下提高基於LLM的BioRE的可靠性。跨多個基準、模型系列和截止後文獻的結果支持ANCHOR-RE作為一種實用的無需訓練的生物醫學文獻挖掘方法。
